# fix: convert timeout from milliseconds to seconds in Python SDK ## Summary Fixes a critical bug where timeout values in the Python SDK were documented as milliseconds but passed directly to `requests.post(timeout=...)` which expects seconds. This caused timeouts to be 1000x longer than intended (e.g., a 60-second timeout became 16.6 hours, effectively disabling client-side timeouts). **Changes made:** - Fixed timeout conversion in `FirecrawlApp.scrape_url()` method (line 596) - Fixed timeout conversion in `FirecrawlApp._post_request()` method (line 2207) - Added comprehensive tests covering both methods and edge cases - Resolves issue #1848 **Impact:** This is a **breaking behavior change** - timeouts will now be significantly shorter than before, matching the documented API behavior. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **CRITICAL:** Test end-to-end with real API calls using various timeout values (e.g., 30000ms should timeout after ~35 seconds, not 8+ hours) - [ ] **CRITICAL:** Run the new tests to confirm they pass: `python -m pytest tests/test_timeout_conversion.py -v` - [ ] **IMPORTANT:** Verify timeout conversion math is correct: `timeout_ms / 1000.0 + 5` gives seconds with 5-second buffer - [ ] **IMPORTANT:** Search codebase for other timeout-related methods that might need similar fixes - [ ] **MEDIUM:** Confirm AsyncFirecrawlApp class doesn't have similar timeout issues (I believe it uses aiohttp differently) **Recommended test plan:** Create a simple script that calls `app.scrape_url()` with `timeout=10000` (10 seconds) and verify it actually times out after ~15 seconds, not 2.7+ hours. --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD Issue["GitHub Issue #1848

Session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/da2ef49f330446fab4e137bfaf2d2e82 - **Testing limitation:** I was unable to run tests locally due to missing dependencies (pydantic, etc.), so the tests need to be verified by CI/human review - **AsyncFirecrawlApp:** This class uses aiohttp with different timeout handling and doesn't appear to have the same bug, but worth double-checking - **Backward compatibility:** Existing code relying on the incorrect (very long) timeout behavior may break, but this aligns with documented API behavior --- ## Summary by cubic Fixed a bug in the Python SDK where timeout values were incorrectly passed as milliseconds instead of seconds, causing requests to wait much longer than intended. - **Bug Fixes** - Updated `scrape_url` and `_post_request` methods to convert timeout from milliseconds to seconds with a 5-second buffer. - Added tests to verify correct timeout handling and edge cases.
